commitResults.messageBody:
Some command offsets use raw numbers, and two task collections have
singular names. These choices obscure their intent.

Derive offsets from command text, separate logical field groups, and
give collections plural names. This improves readability without
changing application behavior.

Users need a faster way to locate tasks in long lists.

Add a case-insensitive find command that searches task descriptions and shows matches in their original order. Reject empty keywords so malformed commands do not accidentally match every task.

Add the official SE-EDU Checkstyle configuration and make existing source and test formatting comply, so style violations become part of the repeatable Gradle quality checks.
Make the course Checkstyle rules and compliant formatting part of the main development baseline before adding the GUI.

Introduce a responsive FXML chat interface with original avatars while sharing command execution, persistence, and response formatting with the console UI. Add focused tests for the GUI-facing response API and keep runtime task data out of version control.
Make the verified graphical interface and shared command-response path the new development baseline while preserving the console UI.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use varargs for console response lines
commitResults.messageBody: Centralize ordered multi-line output in one focused helper and cover the rendered boundary and blank-line behavior with a regression test.
Keep console response rendering concise and verified while preserving the established output format.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assertions for internal state assumptions
commitResults.messageBody:
Parsed commands carry data that is required by only one command type.
Task numbers must also remain valid after they are checked.

Assert these internal invariants so programming errors fail early during
development without replacing user-facing error handling.

Command matching repeats the same boundary checks in several places.
Task subclasses also duplicate constructor initialization, while Geek
retains an exception branch that Parser already handles.

These repetitions make the control flow harder to read and create more
places that must remain consistent when the code changes.

Extract command matching and use early returns in Parser. Delegate task
constructors to one initialization path, and remove the unreachable
exception handler from Geek.

Task-list formatting manually builds numbered output with a loop.
Date-time formatter creation also uses loops to transform and combine
fixed pattern lists.

These operations describe collection transformations and can be
expressed more directly with streams while preserving order.

Use IntStream and joining to format numbered tasks. Use map and
flatMap to build the immutable formatter lists, and add a regression
test for multi-task formatting.
Add assertions for internal state assumptions
Improve command parsing code quality
Use streams for collection transformations

Console responses pass multi-line text to println as a single string.
Embedded line feeds remain LF on Windows while println adds CRLF, causing
the platform-specific UI test to fail.

Split responses into logical lines before printing them so every line
uses the platform line separator.
Add a sort command that orders deadlines by due time and events by start time while keeping undated tasks last. Persist the new order and document and test the behavior.
Add chronological task sorting
Accept harmless whitespace and give specific feedback for unexpected arguments and duplicate delimiters.
Improve malformed command handling
Cover corrupted storage, load and save failures, invalid task numbers, and invalid calendar dates through the shared command-response interface.
Expand end-to-end error handling tests
